decision: This review distinguishes pond culture, household consumption/source reports, market supply, and river capture. Species named in fishpond production or food-consumption research are not thereby verified as wild or currently present in MMORS rivers. Keep aquaculture and wild-occurrence evidence separate; do not infer safety or legal catchability.

sources.title: Assessment of fish and shellfish consumption of coastal barangays along the Marilao-Meycauayan-Obando River System (MMORS), Philippines

accessAndReuse.access: UPLB repository metadata and an author-uploaded full-text copy were reviewed; no local snapshot or hash retained.
accessAndReuse.reuse: No item-specific open license was established. Only attributed factual summaries are retained; tables, figures, and article text are not reproduced.

methodsAndScope.studyType: Household food-consumption assessment and fishery/aquaculture context, not a taxonomic fish survey.
methodsAndScope.studySites: Three fishing barangays in Meycauayan City and two in Obando, Bulacan; individual barangay names are not supplied in the reviewed text.

reportedProductionAndSupply.context: Reported as traditionally grown in modular fishponds along the Meycauayan and Obando Rivers; aquaculture context, not river capture identification.
Reported as traditionally grown in modular fishponds along the Meycauayan and Obando Rivers; aquaculture context, not river capture identification.
Reported as pond production; crustacean, not a fish species.

sourceSeparation: The article describes both pond-grown produce and household-reported own harvest, but does not link individual fish taxa to a specific wild-capture event or site.
Most listed purchase routes include wet markets, small markets, vendors, and neighbors; the text states that some produce is sourced outside Bulacan and may be mixed at markets.
The reported household-consumption species list must not be interpreted as an MMORS wild-fish checklist.

sources.title: Microplastics in Sediments and Fishes of the Marilao-Meycauayan-Obando River System, Bulacan, Philippines
sources.author: Cherry Ann A. Gorgonio

accessAndReuse.access: UPLB library thesis-list abstract reviewed; full manuscript, detailed methods, and item-level reuse terms were not available in the reviewed source.
accessAndReuse.reuse: No permission to redistribute the thesis or derive public app content was established.

scopeAndMethods.studyType: Abstract describes a downstream-MMORS microplastics baseline study involving river/pond sediments and two pond-culture fish species.
scopeAndMethods.speciesSampling: The abstract identifies cultured fish but does not provide collection dates, exact sampling coordinates, sample counts, source ponds, or voucher information.

reportedCulturedFish.context: Pond-culture fish in the thesis abstract; not a wild river occurrence record.
Pond-culture fish in the thesis abstract; this does not establish a wild MMORS occurrence or invasive status.

limitations: The 2017 study is a food-system and household-consumption study; its interviews and questionnaire do not substitute for voucher-backed fish sampling.
Neither source supplies sufficient per-taxon coordinates and dates to establish a current wild distribution in the named rivers.
Fishpond or market production may be geographically connected to river water without being evidence of naturally occurring fish in that river.
The 2017 study reports that some products are sourced outside the case areas and mixed during distribution; local consumption cannot establish local origin.
No source-specific reuse license was confirmed for either publication.
nextStep: Continue seeking a recent, taxon-resolved wild-capture survey for Bulacan's named rivers and inland waters. Keep pond-culture and market-supply evidence in separate categories and require sampling dates, locality, method, taxonomic support, and reuse review before any public occurrence claim.
